name: Wu Rongguang
current_role: Founder and Chairman (behind the scenes) of Hongxing Erke Group (ERKE sportswear), Quanzhou/Xiamen, China
profile: Wu Rongguang took over his father Wu Hanjie's Fujian shoe factory (Hongxing Shoes) in 2000 and registered the Hongxing Erke brand that June, building it into one of China's best-known domestic sportswear labels. His younger brother Wu Rongzhao became CEO in 2007; Wu Rongguang moved to chairman and then behind the scenes, running Hongxing Erke (Xiamen) Investment, which focuses on health-sector investments.
interesting_fact: ERKE went viral in July 2021 after pledging 50 million yuan in goods and cash for Henan flood relief despite thin profits, triggering a nationwide 'buy ERKE' wave that emptied its livestreams and stores.
deep_cut_fact: The brand was born out of the 1997 Asian financial crisis: as export orders to Jinjiang shoe factories collapsed, Wu converted his father's OEM shoe business into an own-brand company, surviving an early cash crunch.
notes: Very low public profile; brother Wu Rongzhao is the public face of ERKE. Best route is via Hongxing Erke corporate PR (Xiamen). Sources are Chinese-language.

name: Sanjeev Kumar Bijli
current_role: Executive Director, PVR INOX Limited (India's largest multiplex chain)
profile: Sanjeev Kumar Bijli co-founded PVR with his brother Ajay in 1995 as a joint venture between the family's Priya Cinemas and Australia's Village Roadshow, pioneering India's multiplex era. Long-time Joint MD, he oversees programming, Hollywood studio relationships and the PVR Pictures distribution arm; since the 2023 PVR-INOX merger he is Executive Director of PVR INOX.
interesting_fact: The 'PVR' name comes from Priya Cinemas (the Bijli family's single-screen theatre in Delhi) plus Village Roadshow, the Australian partner in the original 1995 joint venture.
deep_cut_fact: He has attended Cannes and the Marché du Film for nearly two decades buying indie films for PVR Pictures (Miramax, A24, StudioCanal titles), and admits he 'genuinely didn't know anime had such a big market in India' before PVR's Suzume and Demon Slayer releases.
notes: Input name 'Sanjeev Kumar' = Sanjeev Kumar Bijli. Gives frequent trade-press interviews (Hollywood Reporter India, Bollywood Hungama); media-friendly. Energy/data-centre angle weak.

name: Surendralal Lanca (Lal) Karsanbhai
current_role: President & CEO, Emerson Electric Co. (EMR); Director, Merck & Co.
profile: Lal Karsanbhai joined Emerson in 1995 as an international planner after his Washington University MBA and rose through corporate planning and the Automation Solutions business, which he led from 2018. CEO since February 2021, he has reshaped Emerson into a pure-play industrial automation and software company (selling Climate Technologies, buying AspenTech and NI). He also sits on Merck's board.
interesting_fact: He was born outside the US, moved country to country with his father's job, and did not learn English until age 10, before coming to the US for an economics degree at the University of Michigan.
deep_cut_fact: He is a vinyl enthusiast who unwinds listening to LP records, and named Tower Grove's iNDO as a favourite St. Louis restaurant in a 2022 profile.
notes: Strong fit for energy/automation theme (Emerson serves power, LNG, data-centre controls). Media requests go through FleishmanHillard per Emerson's newsroom.

name: Glade M. Knight
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Apple Hospitality REIT, Inc. (APLE), Richmond, VA
profile: Utah-born, BYU-educated (BA, MBA) real estate entrepreneur who built the 'Apple' family of non-traded REITs and earlier ran Cornerstone Realty Income Trust (1993-2005). He founded Apple Hospitality, a lodging REIT owning Marriott- and Hilton-branded select-service hotels, was CEO until 2014 when his son Justin took over, and remains Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: He is the founding figure of Southern Virginia University, which he reorganised in the 1990s and chaired from 1996 to 2015; its stadium bears the Knight name.
deep_cut_fact: A competitive horseman with ranches in Virginia and Texas, he offered SVU students a yearly 'Cowboy Up' scholarship honouring his father 'Mac' Knight, whom he calls 'my champion and the real cowboy'; the campus knight statue bears Mac's likeness.
notes: Born 1944; low media profile. Wikipedia notes an LDS patriarch role and close friendship with Bill Marriott. Avoid referencing the 2014 SEC disclosure fines.

name: Bruce C. Bruckmann
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director, Bruckmann, Rosser, Sherrill & Co. (BRS), New York; Director, Mohawk Industries
profile: Harvard College and Harvard Law graduate who practised at Patterson Belknap, then spent 1983-94 at Citicorp Venture Capital before co-founding middle-market private equity firm BRS in 1995 with Harold Rosser and Stephen Sherrill. BRS backed consumer, retail and restaurant companies such as B&G Foods and AMF Bowling; he sits on Mohawk's board and was a long-time H&E Equipment director (H&E was acquired by Herc in 2025).
interesting_fact: The three BRS founders had worked together at Citicorp Venture Capital since as early as 1983 before spinning out their own firm in 1995 and putting their surnames on the door.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was a lawyer: an associate at New York firm Patterson, Belknap, Webb & Tyler after Harvard Law School.
notes: Very private PE investor; no published personal or press email found. Best route is via BRS's main office or Mohawk Industries' corporate secretary. Current BRS title not reconfirmed on brs.com (site blocked automated access).

name: Rajesh Agarwal
profile: A mechanical engineer and former IT salesman (Pertech, Xerox), Rajesh Agarwal co-founded Micromax with Rahul Sharma, Sumit Arora and Vikas Jain, growing it from an IT/training business into India's top domestic phone brand in the late 2000s on cheap dual-SIM handsets. Micromax has since pivoted toward electronics manufacturing and memory chips (MiPhi JV with Phison) under Rahul Sharma.
interesting_fact: Micromax broke into handsets with dual-SIM phones when critics predicted it would 'end up losing big time'; Agarwal says 'We wouldn't be in business had we not created a category.'
deep_cut_fact: In 1991 he sold his Maruti 800 for Rs 80,000 to fund his first venture, a PC-assembly firm called Micromax Technologies; he later co-founded Micromax Informatics with Rahul Sharma, his neighbour of 35 years.
notes: Low public profile versus co-founder Rahul Sharma. No published personal/press email found; route via Micromax corporate. Current executive role not confirmed in 2026 sources.

name: Pranay Godha
current_role: Managing Director & CEO, Ipca Laboratories Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Pranay Godha leads Ipca Laboratories, the Indian drugmaker (APIs, formulations, notably anti-malarials and pain management) his father Premchand Godha has steered since 1975. Ipca posted FY26 revenue of about Rs 9,646 crore with over half earned abroad; Premchand is executive chairman and brother Prashant is an executive director.
interesting_fact: Ipca was rescued from losses in 1975 by a group including chartered accountant Premchand Godha (Pranay's father) and actor Amitabh Bachchan's family; the Bachchans sold their 36% stake to the directors in 1997, leaving the Godhas in control.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.Sc. from the University of Bombay and an MBA from the New York Institute of Technology, and came up through marketing and general management at Ipca.
notes: Low media profile; company comms via Ipca corporate (Kandivli, Mumbai). Investor-relations email is published in Ipca's annual reports/stock-exchange filings but could not be extracted (search budget exhausted).

name: Rex D. Geveden
current_role: President & CEO, BWX Technologies (BWXT); Director, TTM Technologies
profile: Kentucky-born engineering physicist who rose from satellite project manager to NASA Chief Engineer and Associate Administrator (2005-07), then ran Teledyne Brown Engineering and Teledyne DALSA. He joined BWXT as COO in 2015 and has been CEO since 2017, leading the naval-reactor and nuclear-fuel supplier into what he calls 'a multi-decadal investment cycle' in nuclear energy and security.
interesting_fact: NASA administrator Mike Griffin created the Associate Administrator post for him in 2005, saying 'if you get a decision from Rex, it's the agency's decision,' and later praised 'one of the most agile minds I have encountered'.
deep_cut_fact: At NASA Marshall he was project manager for Gravity Probe B, the satellite that confirmed Einstein's frame-dragging prediction, as well as the Lightning Imaging Sensor and Optical Transient Detector; he holds physics degrees from Murray State (Sigma Pi Sigma).

name: Jason Robins
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, DraftKings Inc. (DKNG), Boston
profile: Former Vistaprint analytics executive who co-founded DraftKings in 2012 with colleagues Matt Kalish and Paul Liberman. He took it from daily fantasy sports to the largest US-based vertically integrated sports betting and iGaming operator, and in 2026 is pushing into prediction markets; DraftKings says 1.6M+ customers used its Predictions product year-to-date in Q3 2026.
interesting_fact: In April 2013 Major League Baseball invested in DraftKings, the first US pro league to invest in daily fantasy sports.
deep_cut_fact: DraftKings started out of co-founder Paul Liberman's house, and its very first product was a one-on-one fantasy baseball contest timed to launch on MLB Opening Day 2012.
notes: Active on LinkedIn and X personally (handles not verified here). Media-savvy; route via Media@draftkings.com. Avoid referencing the 2024 SEC Reg FD matter tied to his social posts.

name: Chris Diorio, Ph.D.
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Vice Chair, Impinj, Inc. (PI), Seattle
profile: Caltech-trained electrical engineer (BA physics, Occidental) who co-founded Impinj in 2000 with his PhD adviser Carver Mead, commercialising their research. Impinj makes RAIN (UHF RFID) chips and readers that tag billions of retail and logistics items. CEO since 2014, he reported record endpoint IC revenue in Q3 2026 on its M800 chips; he remains an affiliate professor of CSE at the University of Washington.
interesting_fact: The company name is a technical acronym: Impinj stands for 'Impact-ionized hot-electron injection', the semiconductor effect behind the Caltech research by Mead and Diorio.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Impinj he consulted for it (2000-04) and served as VP Engineering and CTO; he also chaired the RAIN Alliance industry group and sits on GS1's Innovation Board and the EPCglobal Board of Governors that set RFID standards.

ir@impinj.com (Andy Cobb, VP Corporate Finance & IR)

name: John W. Childs
current_role: Chairman, J.W. Childs Associates, FL L.P. (West Palm Beach); Director, Biohaven Ltd. and VeraDermics

Childs Associates in 1995; at 84 its focus has shifted to early-stage biotech, pharma and health consumer investments, and he sits on the Biohaven and VeraDermics boards.

current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, DuPont de Nemours, Inc. (DD)
profile: A finance executive who joined DuPont (EID) in 2008 as a global finance manager, Lori Koch ran investor relations and FP&A, became CFO in February 2020 and CEO on June 1, 2024. name: Stefan J. Murry, Ph.D.
current_role: Chief Financial Officer (since 2014) and Chief Strategy Officer (since 2012), Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. (AAOI), Sugar Land, TX
profile: University of Houston physicist and electrical engineer (BS, MS, PhD) who joined AOI in 1997 as a senior device-packaging engineer, then ran sales and marketing before becoming CSO and CFO. AOI makes optical transceivers and lasers for hyperscale data centres and cable TV; Murry is driving its capacity build-out (approaching 330,000 units/month in Q3 2026) as AI data-centre demand surges.
